<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pension costs</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Contributions
to defined contribution pension schemes are charged to the profit and loss
account in the year in which they become payable.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investments</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investments
are stated at cost less any provision for a permanent diminution in value.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating leases</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Annual
rentals on operating leases are charged to the profit and loss account on a
straight line basis over the term of the lease.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employee benefit trust</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The group is deemed to have
control of the assets, liabilities, income and costs of its Employee Benefit
Trust (EBT). It has therefore been included in the financial statements of the
company in accordance with UITF 32 &#147;Employee benefit trusts and other
intermediate payment arrangements&#148;.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Contributions
made to the Trust are charged to the profit and loss account to the extent that
the assets held by the Trust as a result of the contribution have been
unconditionally gifted to the beneficiaries or, if earlier, when a constructive
obligation has arisen and created a liability of the company. The value of any
assets held by the Trust that have not been unconditionally transferred to
beneficiaries is included within cash. In accordance with FRS 12 &#147;Provisions,
Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets&#148;, constructive obligations to
employees in respect of past services to the business have been charged to the
profit and loss account in the period to which they relate.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Government grants</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Grants relating to expenditure
on tangible fixed assets are credited to the profit and loss account at the
same rate as the depreciation on the assets to which the grant relates. The
deferred element of grants is included in creditors as deferred income.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Grants
of a revenue nature are credited to the profit and loss account in the year to
which they relate.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Research and
development</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Expenditure on pure and applied research is charged to
the profit and loss account in the year in which it is incurred.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Development costs
are also charged to the profit and loss account in the year of expenditure, unless
individual projects satisfy all of the following criteria:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>the
project is clearly defined and related expenditure is separately identifiable;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>the
project is technically feasible and commercially viable;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>current
and future costs are expected to be exceeded by future sales; and</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>adequate
resources exist for the project to be completed.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In such circumstances the
costs are carried forward and amortised over a period not exceeding
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; years commencing in the year the group starts to
benefit from the expenditure.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Foreign Currency</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Transactions in foreign
currencies are recorded at the rate ruling at the date of the transaction or at
the contracted rate if the transaction is covered by a forward foreign currency
contract. Monetary assets </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">70</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='70',FILE='C:\fc\759652930_D11265_931049\3298-1-gi.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 16 09:07 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">and
liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are retranslated at the rate of
exchange ruling at the balance sheet date or if appropriate at the forward
contract rate. All differences are taken to the profit and loss account.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
financial statements of overseas subsidiary undertakings are translated at the
rate of exchange ruling on the balance sheet date. The Exchange difference
arising on the retranslation of opening net assets is taken directly to
reserves.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dividends</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
accordance with FRS 21 &#147;Events after the balance sheet date&#148;, dividends
declared after the balance sheet date are not recognised as a liability at the
balance sheet date.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Turnover</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Analysis
by geographical area:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Factors that may
affect future tax charges:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The group has tax losses of
&#163;405,683 that are available for offset against future taxable profits of those
companies in which the losses arose.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">No
deferred tax is recognised on the unremitted earnings of overseas subsidiaries
as the group has no liability to additional taxation should such amounts be
remitted due to the availability of double taxation relief.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Dividends</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Included
with accruals and deferred income is an amount of &#163;135,000 (2004 - &#163;225,000) in
relation to government grants not yet released to the profit and loss account. The
grants may become liable to be repaid if the group breaches certain criteria
during the period of the grants.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There
was an unprovided deferred tax asset at 31 December&nbsp;2004 of &#163;108,775. This
related to unutilised trading losses. This asset was not recognised in the
accounts as the group did not anticipate making sufficient taxable profits in
the near future to absorb the underlying timing differences.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The company has implemented FRS 21 &#147;Events after the
balance sheet date&#148; during the year ended 31&nbsp;December 2005. Accordingly,
dividends declared after the balance sheet date are no longer recognised as a
liability at the balance sheet date. As a consequence, the profit and loss
account and shareholders funds at 31&nbsp;December 2003 were increased by
&#163;138,379.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">20</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Acquisitions</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following acquisitions were
made in the year to 31 December&nbsp;2003:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Acquisition of assets of the Deutsche Bank AG New
York Branch Horsham.</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On 3&nbsp;February 2003, the company purchased the
assets of the Deutsche Bank AG New York Branch Horsham, which provided software
development services to Deutsche Bank AG New York. The total consideration was </font><font face="Times New Roman">&#128;</font>3,000,000 (&#163;1,761,389)
and is payable in six instalments ending 3&nbsp;August 2005.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">23</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Pension costs</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
group contributes to defined contribution pension schemes. The assets of the
schemes are held separately from those of the group in independently
administered funds. The pension cost charge for the year ended 31
December&nbsp;2005 was &#163;829,148 (2004 - &#163;833,666; 2003 - &#163;935,356). The unpaid
pension contributions outstanding at the year end were &#163;99,565 (2004 -
&#163;113,638, 2003 - &#163;105,482).</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">24</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Companies
Act 1985</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These consolidated
accounts do not comprise the company&#146;s &#147;statutory accounts&#148; within the meaning
of section 240 of the Companies Act 1985 of Great Britain. Statutory accounts
for the years ended 30&nbsp;June 2003 and 2004 and 2005 have been delivered to
the Registrar of Companies for England and Wales. The statutory auditors&#146;
reports on such accounts were unqualified.</font></p>

<div>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">25</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Related party transactions</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Kanbay Europe Limited, a
subsidiary of Kanbay International Inc (which owns 49% of the issued share
capital of SSS Holdings Corporation Limited) performed work for the group
during the year ended 31&nbsp;December&nbsp;2005 for which &#163;19,693 (2004&#150;&#163;28,180;
2003&#150;&#163;42,208) was invoiced. There were no outstanding balances due to Kanbay
Europe Limited at 31 December&nbsp;2005 (2004 &#163;nil).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SSS Holdings Corporation
Limited, together with Morgan Stanley and Co International Inc. and the
directors owned 100% of the issued share capital of The Monocle Holdings
Corporation Limited, the ultimate parent company of The Monocle Corporation
Limited. The Monocle Holdings Corporation Limited and The Monocle Corporation
Limited were dissolved in October&nbsp;2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year to 31 December&nbsp;2003 the group
performed work for The Monocle Corporation Limited. &#163;26,000 was invoiced during
the year to 31 December&nbsp;2003 in respect of this work. There were no
amounts due from The Monocle Corporation Limited at 31 December&nbsp;2004. During
the year to 31&nbsp;December 2004, The Monocle Corporation Limited invoiced the
group &#163;7,095 (2004&#150;&#163;7,095; 2003&#150;&#163;6,540). The amount due to The Monocle
Corporation Limited at 31&nbsp;December 2004 was &#163;nil.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year to 31&nbsp;December
2004 the group received computer equipment for &#163;155,309 and cash of &#163;95,668 in
full settlement of the net amounts due from The Monocle Corporation Limited and
the provision of &#163;230,518 recorded in previous years was released to the profit
and loss account.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Until
September&nbsp;2004, SSS Holdings Corporation Limited owned 50% of the share
capital of Strategic Investment Solutions Limited. During the year to 31 December&nbsp;2004,
the group charged a management fee of &#163;10,575 (2003&#150;&#163;10,575) to Strategic
Investment Solutions Limited. The amount outstanding at 31&nbsp;December 2004
was &#163;nil.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">26</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Difference
between United Kingdom and United States Generally Accepted Accounting
Principles</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s consolidated
accounts are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally
accepted in the United Kingdom (&#147;UK GAAP&#148;) which differ from United States
generally accepted accounting principles (&#147;US GAAP&#148;). The significant
differences applicable to the Company are summarised below:</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill and
intangible assets</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under UK GAAP goodwill is amortised on a straight-line
basis over its useful life up to a maximum of 20&nbsp;years. Under US GAAP,
goodwill is not amortised, but is reviewed annually for impairment. Goodwill
amortisation under UK GAAP is reversed for US GAAP purposes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under US GAAP other intangible
assets may be identified when an acquisition occurs before assigning the
remaining purchase price to goodwill. An intangible asset for the customer
relationship was identified for US GAAP accounting related to the acquisition
described in Note&nbsp;21 in the amount of &#163;743,048. This intangible asset will
be amortised over its estimated life of 6&nbsp;years.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accrual for
vacation expense</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under UK GAAP, the group
did not fully provide for vacation expense. Under US GAAP the group would fully
provide for this cost.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Software costs</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under UK GAAP, costs related to purchased software are
expensed to the profit and loss account as incurred. Under US GAAP such costs
are capitalised in the balance sheet and depreciated over their expected useful
lives.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">80</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

2003, 2004 and 2005 and to shareholders&#146; funds as of 31&nbsp;December 2004 and
2005 that would be required if US GAAP were to be applied instead of UK GAAP
together with the statement of comprehensive income that would be required
under US GAAP.</font></p>

 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">81</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Consolidated statement of cash
flows</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The consolidated statement of
cash flows prepared under UK GAAP present substantially the same information as
that required under US GAAP. However, the statements differ with regard to the
classification of items within them and as regards to the definition of cash
under UK GAAP and cash and cash equivalents under US GAAP.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under UK GAAP, cash flows are
presented separately for operating activities, returns on investments and
servicing of finance, taxation, capital expenditure and financial investment,
acquisitions, equity dividends and management of liquid resources and
financing. US GAAP requires only three categories of cash flow to be reported;
operating, investing and financing. Cash flows from taxation and returns on
investments and servicing shown under UK GAAP would, with the exception of
dividends paid to minority shareholders, be included within operating
activities under US GAAP. The payment of dividends would be included as a
financing activity under US GAAP. Capital expenditure and financial investment
and acquisitions are reported within investing activities under US GAAP. Under
US GAAP, cash and cash equivalents include short-term highly liquid investments
but do not include bank overdrafts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The categories of cash flow activity under US GAAP can
be summarised as follows:</font></p>

<div align="center">

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="a06-3298_110k.htm#Item9a_ControlsAndProcedures__092538">Item&nbsp;9.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Changes in and Disagreements with
Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure</a><a name="Item9_ChangesInAndDisagreementsWi_092532"></a>.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item9a_ControlsAndProcedures__092538"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="a06-3298_110k.htm#Item9b_OtherInformation_092528">Item&nbsp;9A.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Controls and Procedures</a>.</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="EvaluationOfDisclosureControlsAnd_012315"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Evaluation
of Disclosure Controls and Procedures and Changes in Internal Control over
Financial Reporting</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, our Chief Executive
Officer and Chief Financial Officer evaluated the effectiveness of our
disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and
15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended). Based
on their evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures, our Chief
Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, with the participation of our
management, have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures are
effectively designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by us
in the reports that we file or submit under the Securities Exchange Act of
1934, as amended, is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the
time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#146;s rules&nbsp;and
forms and are operating in an effective manner.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There were no changes in our
internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rule&nbsp;13a-15(f)
of the Exchange Act) during the fourth quarter of 2005 that materially
affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control
over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ManagementsReportOnInternalContro_012316"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management&#146;s
Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management is responsible for the preparation,
integrity and fair presentation of the consolidated financial statements and
notes to the consolidated financial statements. The financial statements were
prepared in accordance with the accounting principles generally accepted in the
U.S. and include certain amounts based on management&#146;s judgment and best
estimates. Other financial information presented is consistent with the
financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management is also
responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over
financial reporting as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;and 15d-15(f)
under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The Company&#146;s internal control over
financial reporting is designed under the supervision of the Company&#146;s
principal executive and financial officers in order to provide reasonable
assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation
of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally
accepted accounting principles. The Company&#146;s internal control over financial
reporting includes those policies and procedures that:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(i)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Pertain to the
maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly
reflect the transactions and dispositions of assets of the Company;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(ii)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Provide reasonable
assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of
financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting
principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the Company are being made
only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the
Company; and</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(iii)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Provide reasonable assurance
regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or
disposition of the Company&#146;s assets that could have a material effect on the
financial statements.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control
over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also,
projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to
the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions,
or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may
deteriorate.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">83</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='83',FILE='C:\fc\7510735600_D11265_931309\3298-1-ha.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 16 10:07 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management assessed the effectiveness of the Company&#146;s
internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2005. In
making this assessment, management used the criteria established in Internal
Control&#151;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring
Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company completed its acquisitions of Accurum,&nbsp;Inc.
and Pune Software Park Private Limited on March&nbsp;1, 2005 and
October&nbsp;19, 2005, respectively. As permitted by the U.S. Securities and
Exchange Commission, management&#146;s assessment as of December&nbsp;31, 2005 did
not include the internal control of Accurum, Inc. and Pune Software Park
Private Limited, which are included in the Company&#146;s consolidated financial
statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2005. Accurum, Inc. constituted $13,019 and
$1,193 of total and net assets, respectively, as of December&nbsp;31, 2005 and
$12,692 and $1,193 of revenues and net income, respectively, for the year then
ended. Pune Software Park Private Limited constituted $4,831 and ($31) of total
and net assets, respectively, as of December&nbsp;31, 2005 and $0 and $(31) of
revenues and net income (loss), respectively, for the year then ended. (All
numbers referenced above for Accurum, Inc. and Pune Software Park Private
Limited are stated in thousands.)</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Based on management&#146;s assessment, which excluded an
assessment of internal control over financial reporting of the acquired operations
of Accurum,&nbsp;Inc. and Pune Software Park Private Limited, management has
concluded that the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting was
effective as of December&nbsp;31, 2005 to provide reasonable assurance
regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of
financial statements for external reporting purposes in accordance with GAAP.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s independent registered public accounting
firm, Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP, has issued an attestation report on
management&#146;s assessment of the Company&#146;s internal control over financial
reporting. That report appears on a preceeding page&nbsp;of this Report and
expresses unqualified opinions on management&#146;s assessment and on the
effectiveness of the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Kanbay International,&nbsp;Inc.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">March&nbsp;14, 2006</font></p>
